theater: 都柏林郡斯凱里與克朗道爾金

battle.name: 維京人入侵愛爾蘭
battle.theater: 都柏林郡斯凱里與克朗道爾金
battle.brief: 795年，一支北歐私掠船隊首次踏上愛爾蘭，在都柏林灣北岸洗劫聖帕特里克教堂與首領的堡壘，隨即被達爾里亞的艦隊逐走。卡面的埃及長矛是青銅時代造價最低的刺擊兵器，千年後仍是步戰最普遍的近身武器；本役攻守雙方都無攻城器械，勝負全押在船隊、盾牆與長矛之上。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 交戰的兩方是北歐峽灣的私掠船隊與愛爾蘭的土著王權，第三方則是蘇格蘭的蓋爾語王國達爾里亞。795年的愛爾蘭並無中央政權，島上分為芒斯特、倫斯特、烏爾斯特、康諾特與米埃五個省，各有王系，中部平原另設至高王庭；沿海散布著大大小小的氏族領地（túath）與各自的木柵堡壘。北愛爾蘭自7世紀起屢遭北不列顛的加冕王攻掠，682、698、705、716年的戰事迫使大批教會人員與貴族北逃阿蓋爾，愛爾蘭的海岸防線因此更加空疏。來犯者並非任何國家的軍隊，而是自備船隻與夥伴的挪威海商與戰士團，臨時編成甲板戰鬥隊，沒有旗號、沒有徵召令、沒有後方基地。守方以修道院壁壘為核心：石砌教堂帶內院圍牆、壕溝與門樓，圍牆內的守軍由常駐的武裝僧侶與地方民兵組成，武器以長矛、斧與圓盾為主。北歐方面完全沒有攻城裝備，攻守兩端都靠人力與船隻。
countriesEn: The two sides in this were the private war-band of the Norse fjord lords and the native Irish kingship, with a third party, the Gaelic kingdom of Dál Riata in Scotland. Ireland in 795 had no central government: the island was divided into the five provinces of Munster, Leinster, Ulster, Connacht and Mide, each with its own dynasty, while a separate high kingship sat in the plain of the central plain; along the coasts lay a scatter of petty lordships (túath) and their wooden palisaded strongholds. Northern Ireland had been repeatedly struck by the crowned kings of Northumbria since the seventh century, and the campaigns of 682, 698, 705 and 716 had driven great numbers of clergy and nobles north into Argyll, leaving Ireland's coastal defence all the thinner. The attackers were not the army of any state but a trading-and-raiding war-band of Norwegian sea-traders and warriors, mustered ad hoc on deck, without banners, without a levy and without any base in the rear. The defenders were organised around the fortified monasteries: stone churches with an enclosed yard, a ditch and a gatehouse, manned by armed monks and local militia whose weapons were primarily spear, axe and round shield. The Norse side had no siege equipment whatsoever, and both ends of the fighting turned on muscle and on ships.
people: 795年的事件沒有留下任何主角的名字，愛爾蘭編年史只以「外來人」一詞指稱來犯者，這種無名的記法本身就說明了事件的性質。守方同樣匿名：聖帕特里克教堂的守護者、克朗道爾金一帶首領的堡壘守軍，史料都沒有留下名字。唯一可以合理指認的關鍵人物，是皮克特國王兼達爾里亞之主奧恩古斯一世（Oengus，約730年生，812年卒），他自780年起執掌達爾里亞，並自778年起接納北逃的愛爾蘭流亡者，編年史所記的「被達爾里亞擊敗」很可能指他的艦隊在海上攔截了入侵者。愛爾蘭本土方面，795年時的至高王是歐查德·麥克·博因（在位780至797年），北線的烏伊·奈爾直到797年才由艾德·奧德尼德接掌塔拉王位，編年史並未記載任何一位愛爾蘭君王在795年直接出戰。記載者本身也是人物：12世紀的《提格納赫編年史》、14世紀的《烏爾斯特編年史》，以及1630年代由邁克爾·奧克萊里等人在都柏林完成的《四統治者編年史》，三者的795年條目正是今日重建此役的基礎。17世紀的愛爾蘭古物學者才首先辨認出編年史裡的「撒克遜人」其實是北歐人。
peopleEn: No name survives from the event of 795. The Irish annalists refer to the attackers only as foreigners, and this anonymity is itself a statement about the nature of the episode. The defenders are equally nameless: the custodian of St Patrick's church and the garrison of the chiefs' strongholds around Cluain Dolcain are not named in any source. The only key figure who can reasonably be identified is Oengus, king of the Picts and ruler of Dál Riata (c. 730–812), who held Dál Riata from 780 and who had been harbouring Irish exiles since 778; the annalistic phrase that the raiders were defeated by the Dalriada most probably points to his fleet intercepting them at sea. On the Irish side of the fighting, the high king in 795 was Eochaid mac Bóinne (r. 780–797), and the northern Uí Néill only took the kingship of Tara with Áed Oirdnide in 797; no Irish king is recorded as having personally fought in 795. The recorders are themselves part of the cast: the twelfth-century Annals of Tigernach, the fourteenth-century Ulster Chronicle, and the Annals of the Four Masters, completed in Dublin by Michael O'Clery and his collaborators in the 1630s. Their entries for 795 are the basis on which the episode is reconstructed today. It was seventeenth-century Irish antiquaries who first identified the 'Saxons' of the annals as Norsemen.
kits: 卡面兵器是一支早王朝時期的埃及長矛：銅或青銅矛頭，葉形或菱形刃，套接式柄口，裝在約兩公尺長的木杆上，杆尾常加尾錐，屬青銅時代最普遍、造價最低的刺擊兵器。必須說清楚的是，這件兵器本身並未出現在795年的愛爾蘭，它在卡牌體系裡的位置是「刺擊長矛」的原型與源頭——從早王朝的埃及方陣矛兵，一路承接到北歐與愛爾蘭戰士手上那支最寒酸的武器。795年的實際裝備：北歐戰士用單刃劍（刀身單側開鋒、劍尖漸收）、斧、圓盾（木板拼製、蒙皮、油漆或彩繪圖案）、弓箭與長矛，多數矛頭為木製或包骨，鐵矛頭則是自挪威運來的貴重物；愛爾蘭一方以長矛、短矛、斧、投石索與圓盾為主，木盾以木條與皮革拼製。守軍另有柳條編織的護牆、土壘與拒馬。攻城方面雙方皆無塔車、撞車與投石器，修道院只靠石牆、高塔、壕溝與門樓拖延來犯者；進攻方能倚仗的只有船隻、速度與人數。船上的划槳手同樣以矛與斧武裝，接舷時的肉搏就是一場密集的矛刺。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is an early dynastic Egyptian spear: a copper or bronze point with a leaf-shaped or lozenge-shaped blade and a socketed tang, fitted to a wooden shaft roughly two metres long and often finished with a butt-spike. It was the most common and the cheapest thrusting weapon of the Bronze Age. It must be said plainly that this weapon itself never reached Ireland in 795; its place in the card system is that of the archetype and ancestor of the thrusting spear, running in an unbroken line from the spearmen of the Egyptian early dynastic phalanx down to the shabbiest weapon in the hands of Norse and Irish warriors. The equipment actually used in 795: Norse warriors carried single-edged swords (a blade sharpened on one side with a tapering point), axes, round shields (planked wood, covered in hide, painted or decorated), bows and spears, most spearheads being of wood or bone while iron heads were a costly import brought from Norway; the Irish side relied on long spears, short spears, axes, slings and round shields, with wooden shields assembled from staves and hide. The garrison had also wicker hurdles, earthen banks and caltrops to work with. On the siege side there was nothing at all: no tower, no battering ram, no artillery on either side, and the monasteries could only slow the raiders with stone walls, towers, ditches and gatehouses. All the attackers had to rely on was their ships, their speed and their numbers. The oarsmen aboard were armed with spear and axe as well, and boarding fights were dense exchanges of thrusting spears.
tactics: 795年這類行動屬於北歐掠奪的早期形態：打了就跑，而非9世紀中葉以後的扎營清剿。船隊由挪威峽灣出發，經設得蘭、奧克尼，沿蘇格蘭西岸南下，穿越愛爾蘭海，最遠可繞到克里西南方外海的斯凱利格島；5月至9月是西風帶航行的季節，可供進攻的窗口也隨之而來。登陸多選在缺乏城牆、難以預警的灘地，例如斯凱里外側的沙岸與蘭貝島的東岸；船隻拖上岸，戰士以甲板為集合點，盾牌與長矛留在船中待發，划槳手用矛應戰。奪取教會的金銀器皿、福音書的金屬鑲飾、穀物與牲口，以及首領堡壘中的儲藏，即刻登船離去。撤退本來就是計畫的一部分：若守軍集結，掠奪者邊打邊退，寧可損失收成也不戀戰。795年正是如此，來犯者在得手之後被達爾里亞的艦隊追擊驅逐，外國人退去。愛爾蘭守軍以圓盾排成密集的盾牆，長矛自盾隙之間刺出，僧侶與民兵退入教堂內院，以石牆、壕溝與高塔換取時間，等待援兵。達爾里亞的海上攔截是另一套戰術：該王國在8世紀後期以艦隊反覆劫掠北不列顛，808年更在曼島擊敗維京人，顯示北線具備成熟的海上打擊能力，這正是795年擊退來犯者的技術基礎。
tacticsEn: An operation like this belonged to the early phase of Norse raiding: hit and run, not the camp-and-clear warfare that came after the middle of the ninth century. The fleet would sail out of the Norwegian fjords, pass Shetland and Orkney, run down the western coast of Scotland, cross the Irish Sea and, at the far limit, round to the Skellig islands off the south-western coast. The sailing season of the westerlies ran from May to September, and the window for attacking moved with it. Landing was normally made on a beach without walls and without warning, such as the sand strand outside Skerries or the east shore of Lambay. The ships were beached, the warriors mustered on deck, shields and spears kept in the hull until needed, and the oarsmen fought with their spears. The object was to take the church's gold and silver plate, the metalwork of the gospel books, grain and cattle, and the stores held in the chiefs' strongholds, and then get back aboard. Withdrawal was part of the plan from the start: if the defenders gathered, the raiders would fight their way back to the boats, preferring to lose their plunder rather than be drawn into a pitched battle. That is exactly what happened in 795: after taking what they came for, the raiders were pursued and driven off by the fleet of Dál Riata, and the foreigners withdrew. The Irish defenders closed into a dense shield-wall of round shields with spears thrust out through the gaps, while monks and militia fell back into the church yards, buying time behind stone walls, ditches and towers until relief could come. The Dál Riata counter-stroke was a different order of tactic altogether: that kingdom repeatedly raided Northumbria with its fleet in the later eighth century and in 808 beat the Vikings at the Isle of Man, which shows that the northern line possessed a developed capacity for sea warfare, and that capability is the technical basis on which the raiders of 795 were driven away.
data: 關於這一役，愛爾蘭史料幾乎不提供數字，這本身就是最可靠的結論。795年是唯一確定的時間，計年以公元紀元，三部主要編年史——《提格納赫編年史》《烏爾斯特編年史》《四統治者編年史》——都為795年留下條目。地名則有兩種版本：《提格納赫編年史》記為蘭貝島（都柏林郡外海，約北緯53.50度、西經6.13度，距都柏林約25公里），《四統治者編年史》與《烏爾斯特編年史》記為斯凱里（北緯53.41度、西經6.11度）的聖帕特里克教堂，再加上克朗道爾金（北緯53.28度、西經6.25度，距都柏林市中心約12公里）；斯凱里至克朗道爾金直線約16公里，蘭貝島至斯凱里約12公里。兵員、船數、戰損與被擄人數，史料一律不載，後世學者只能以鄰近年份推估：798年掠奪布雷加海岸，807年再至德利與科尼亞特，811年襲福爾，821年兵臨都柏林，841年建立都柏林，而795年距都柏林的建立只有46年。船的形制可參照考古發掘的奧塞堡船（約820年，長21.6公尺、十五對槳）與戈克斯塔德船（約890年，長23.8公尺、十六對槳），但兩者年代都晚於本役，迄今未發現與795年直接相關的沉船。
dataEn: On this campaign the Irish sources supply almost no figures, and that is itself the most reliable conclusion. The year 795 is the one thing that is certain, counted in the Christian era, and all three of the principal chronicles — the Annals of Tigernach, the Ulster Chronicle and the Annals of the Four Masters — carry an entry for it. The place names come in two versions. The Annals of Tigernach record the island of Lambay, off the coast of County Dublin at about 53.50° north, 6.13° west, some 25 kilometres from Dublin; the Annals of the Four Masters and the Ulster Chronicle record the church of St Patrick at Skerries (53.41° north, 6.11° west), together with Cluain Dolcain (53.28° north, 6.25° west), about 12 kilometres from the centre of Dublin. The straight-line distance from Skerries to Cluain Dolcain is roughly 16 kilometres, and from Lambay to Skerries about 12. Numbers of men, of ships, of losses and of captives are simply not recorded, so later scholars can only work forward from the adjacent years: the coast of Brega plundered in 798, Derry and Connacht reached in 807, Fore struck in 811, Dublin threatened in 821, Dublin founded in 841 — 795 stands only 46 years before that foundation. For the form of the ships one may refer to the excavated Oseberg ship (c. 820, 21.6 metres long, fifteen pairs of oars) and the Gokstad ship (c. 890, 23.8 metres, sixteen pairs of oars), but both are later than this action, and no wreck directly connected with 795 has been identified.
cause: 為什麼會打起來，一端是斯堪的納維亞的結構性壓力，一端是愛爾蘭修道院的財富集中。8世紀末的挪威與丹麥面臨人口壓力，以及土地被分割到難以維持氏族份子的局面，年輕的氏族成員需要戰利品、土地與身份；同一時期法蘭克帝國在查理曼率領下向薩克森人與丹麥沿岸施壓，810年的瓦爾赫倫海戰更讓丹麥之王亨姆的艦隊擊敗查理曼的船隊，劫掠因而成為北歐人累積財富與磨練水手的重要手段。而愛爾蘭教會在787年塔拉特會議前後推行告解與苦修的改革，財富集中於少數修道院，地方武力卻近乎空白：金器皿、福音書的寶石鑲嵌、銅製燈臺與聖髮匣具備極高的可攜價值，沿海卻幾乎沒有海防。793年林迪斯法恩之後的第三年，愛爾蘭不過是同一條航線上的下一站，相差僅兩年。入侵是自籌經費的私掠行為，沒有佔領計畫，也沒有後續談判，屬於北歐「貴族式自由企業」的典型形態。
causeEn: Why this happened lies in structural pressure in Scandinavia on one side and in the concentration of Irish church wealth on the other. In the late eighth century Norway and Denmark faced population pressure and a division of land into holdings too small to sustain a kinsman's share, so that younger members of a kindred needed plunder, land and status; at the same time the Frankish empire under Charlemagne was pressing the Saxons and the Danish coast, and the battle of Walcheren in 810, in which the fleet of the Danish king Hemm destroyed Charlemagne's ships, confirmed raiding as a principal means of accumulating wealth and training crews in the north. On the Irish side, the church had pursued penitential and ascetic reform around the council of Tallaght in 787; wealth was concentrated in a handful of monasteries while local armed strength was close to nil. Gold and silver plate, gem-set gospel covers, bronze lamps and reliquaries were both extremely portable in value and, on the coast, entirely undefended. Ireland lay only two years beyond Lindisfarne of 793, the next stop on the same sea route. The attack was a self-financed act of private plunder: no plan for settlement, no subsequent negotiation, and the classic northern form of aristocratic free enterprise.
impact: 795年在編年史裡只是一行字，在愛爾蘭史上卻是一條分水嶺。它是愛爾蘭有記載的第一次北歐掠奪；此後直到1169年諾曼人登陸，愛爾蘭進入長達三百七十餘年的北歐襲擾期，幾乎每十年就有條目記北歐人上岸。短期後果是城市出現：北歐人在841年建立都柏林，隨後是914年的沃特福德與922年的利默里克，愛爾蘭首次有了城牆、市集與市民團體，都柏林更成為北歐式金屬工藝的創作中心，蘭貝島出土的胸針即為代表。教會與學術同樣受衝擊：修道院被洗劫造成手稿與藏書的損失，也推動愛爾蘭修院在9世紀末起向歐陸與英格蘭建立網絡，並在845至847年間出現大批學者外流。政治上，海峽區的北歐據點改變了愛爾蘭諸王的權力計算：都柏林既是外來者的堡壘，也是愛爾蘭王權可以爭奪的資源，11世紀的愛爾蘭王權重組與12世紀末金塞爾的割據衝突，都以此為起點。長期看，795年開啟的北歐—愛爾蘭關係最終與1169年諾曼人的登陸相連：被逐出王位的迪亞爾梅特·麥克·穆爾哈達向英格蘭求援，海峽區的長期存在提供了理由。
impactEn: In the annals 795 is a single line; in Irish history it is a watershed. It is the first recorded Norse raid on Ireland, and it opens a Viking age of plunder and counter-plunder that runs for more than three hundred and seventy years, up to the arrival of the Normans in 1169, with an entry about Norsemen landing appearing roughly every decade. The immediate consequence was the appearance of towns: the Norse founded Dublin in 841, followed by Waterford in 914 and Limerick in 922, and Ireland for the first time had walls, markets and urban communities, with Dublin becoming a centre of northern metalwork whose products are represented by the brooch found on Lambay Island. The church and scholarship were hit as well: the sacking of monasteries cost Ireland manuscripts and libraries, and it pushed Irish houses to build networks across the continent and in England from the late ninth century, with a diaspora of scholars in flight in 845 to 847. Politically, the Norse footholds of the strait region changed how Irish kings calculated power: Dublin was at once a foreign stronghold and a resource Irish kingship could fight for, and both the reorganisation of Irish kingship in the eleventh century and the partition conflict of the late twelfth century in Connacht begin from that ground. In the long run, the Norse-Irish relationship opened in 795 ended in the Norman landing of 1169: Diarmait Mac Murchada, driven from his kingship, appealed to Henry II for intervention, and the long-standing presence of the strait towns supplied the pretext.
result: 795年這一役的直接結果，在《四統治者編年史》裏寫得很清楚：北歐人搶掠了斯凱里與克朗道爾金，被達爾里亞擊敗，外國人退去。沒有城被攻破，沒有據點被建立，愛爾蘭的王權、教會與土地制度毫髮無損，掠奪者帶走財物便回到海上。短期的勝方是愛爾蘭與達爾里亞聯盟的海岸防線，後果只是把襲擊推遲了幾年：798年布雷加海岸、807年德利與科尼亞特、811年福爾、821年都柏林、837年都柏林攻防，腳步一次比一次靠近城市，規模一次比一次大。因此795年同時是終點與起點——它是北歐人第一次被逐走的記錄，也是此後兩百年「年年來、年年退」模式的樣板。值得留意的是它留下的空白：沒有贖金條約，沒有俘虜交換，沒有外交關係，只剩編年史裏一句外國人退去。直到841年北歐人在都柏林立足，這種非對稱的、純粹掠奪式的接觸才第一次轉為長期的政治與軍事關係，而都柏林最終又成為1170年後英格蘭人進入愛爾蘭的落腳點。
resultEn: The immediate result of the campaign of 795 is stated plainly in the Annals of the Four Masters: the Norsemen plundered Skerries and Cluain Dolcain, were defeated by the Dalriada, and the foreigners withdrew. No town was taken, no foothold was established, the Irish kingship, church and land system were left intact, and the raiders sailed away with their loot. The short-term winners were the coastal defences of Ireland and of Dál Riata, and the effect of the victory was merely to postpone the next raids by a few years: the coast of Brega in 798, Derry and Connacht in 807, Fore in 811, Dublin in 821, the fighting over Dublin in 837 — each step nearer the towns, each larger in scale. So 795 is both an end and a beginning: it is the first record of the Norsemen being driven off, and the model for the two centuries of coming every year and leaving every year that followed. What stands out is the emptiness left behind: no ransom treaty, no exchange of prisoners, no diplomatic relation at all, only a line in an annal saying the foreigners withdrew. It was not until the Norse established themselves at Dublin in 841 that this asymmetric, purely predatory contact became a lasting political and military relationship — and Dublin would eventually become the landing place for the English in Ireland after 1170.
